author: B

components.title: Parse and validate version strings
components.what: Split input strings by '.', check that every part is non-empty and contains only decimal digits, and raise ValueError if any check fails.

components.title: Normalize and compare versions
components.what: Convert parts to integers, pad unequal lengths with trailing zeros (using itertools.zip_longest), compare sequentially, and return -1, 0, or 1.

log.author: B

challenges.problem: str.isdecimal() accepts non-ASCII decimal digit characters (e.g. Arabic-Indic '١٢' or Devanagari '१२'), and int() will parse them successfully, so compare_versions('١.٢', '1.2') would not raise ValueError even though the spec implies plain decimal-digit strings (0-9). This is an unsupported inference about what 'decimal digits' means.

str.isdecimal() returns True for non-ASCII decimal digit characters (e.g. Arabic-Indic '١٢٣', fullwidth '１２３', Devanagari digits), which int() will also happily convert. The spec's intent for 'decimal digits' almost certainly means ASCII 0-9; hidden tests may check that such unicode digit strings raise ValueError, but this code will silently accept and parse them.

Unsupported inference: on Python 3.11+, int() raises ValueError for sufficiently long digit strings (typically over 4300 digits) because of the integer string conversion limit, even though those parts consist solely of decimal digits.
